Apply a Review Tracker Back to a Report as a Resolutions Appendix

Source: R/cbe_review_extract.R
apply_review_tracker.Rd

Merges the resolutions of a completed review tracker into a report (`.qmd`, `.Rmd` or `.md`) by appending a "Review resolutions" appendix that records, per tracker item, what was done and where. It is the apply-back step of the review workflow: [docx_review_extract()] extracts comments, [review_tracker()] builds the tracker, [format_review_tracker()] formats it for the response, and this function carries the closed resolutions back into the deliverable.

Usage

apply_review_tracker(tracker, report, output = NULL, overwrite = FALSE)

# S3 method for class 'review_apply'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

tracker

A `cbe_review_tracker` tibble, a data frame with the `status`, `location` and `rationale` columns, or a path to a `.xlsx` or `.csv` tracker file (read as in [validate_review_tracker()]).

report

Path to the `.qmd`, `.Rmd` or `.md` report to append the resolutions appendix to.

output

Path for the report with the appendix. Default: the report name with `_reviewed` before the extension, beside the report.

overwrite

Logical (default `FALSE`): allow `output` to be an existing file. Appending in place (`output` the same file as `report`) also needs `overwrite = TRUE`.

x

The object to print (the result of the function).

...

Not used.

Value

Invisibly, a list of class `review_apply` with `output` (the written path), `applied` (the applied tracker rows), `not_applied` (a tibble with `item_id`, `file`, `status` and `reason`), `n_items` and `n_applied`.

What it does and does not do

A tracker row is *applied* when it is closed (adopted/addressed or not adopted) and records a concrete location or rationale — an adopted row needs a location, a not-adopted row needs a rationale, as checked by [validate_review_tracker()]. Applied rows become the appendix table. Rows that are still open, and closed rows with nothing concrete recorded, are not applied; they are listed under "Not applied" with the reason, so nothing is silently dropped. The function does **not** edit the source `.docx` the comments came from, does **not** change the report body, and does **not** mark tracker rows closed: the appendix is a record of the resolutions, and the edits the tracker describes still have to be made (or verified) in the report by the author. Run [validate_review_tracker()] first when the tracker must be complete before anything is applied.

See also

[review_tracker()], [format_review_tracker()], [validate_review_tracker()]

Examples

tracker <- data.frame(
  item_id = 1:3, file = "manuscript.docx", author = c("Reviewer 1", "Reviewer 2", "Reviewer 1"),
  comment = c("Define the cohort", "Report the sample size", "Check Table 2"),
  status = c("adopted", "not_adopted", "open"),
  location = c("Methods, page 4", "", ""),
  rationale = c("Added the inclusion criteria", "Outside the scope of the study", "")
)
report <- file.path(tempdir(), "report.qmd")
writeLines(c("# Results", "", "The cohort is described here."), report)
res <- apply_review_tracker(tracker, report)
res$n_applied
#> [1] 2
cat(readLines(res$output), sep = "\n")
#> # Results
#> 
#> The cohort is described here.
#> 
#> 
#> ## Review resolutions
#> 
#> Review resolutions applied from the supplied tracker on 2026-11-13: 2 of 3 tracker item(s) are recorded below. The remaining items are listed under “Not applied” and still need a decision. This appendix records what the tracker says was done and where; it does not change the report body and does not edit the source document the comments came from.
#> 
#> | item_id | file | author | comment | status | location | rationale |
#> |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
#> | 1 | manuscript.docx | Reviewer 1 | Define the cohort | adopted | Methods, page 4 | Added the inclusion criteria |
#> | 2 | manuscript.docx | Reviewer 2 | Report the sample size | not_adopted |  | Outside the scope of the study |
#> 
#> ### Not applied
#> 
#> - Item 3 (manuscript.docx): still open: no resolution recorded.
#>
